text: DEFONEOS — DEFRA Natural England AI Deep-Dive Pack EU AI Act Article 50 live 2 Aug 2026 — C2PA passport ready | Get yours → Home Master GovBench Index Sitemap DEFONEOS × DEFRA × NATURAL ENGLAND DEFRA Natural England AI Deep-Dive Pack Sovereign AI governance for Natural England — statutory nature conservation body for England. SSSI monitoring, AONB protection, nature recovery networks, biodiversity net gain, protected species licensing, marine conservation, agri-environment schemes. 12 entry points × 8 transformation priorities × 6 MCPs. Audit-grade. Signed. UK-sovereign. 12 Entry Points 8 Transformation Priorities 6 MCP Servers 6 Red Lines 📋 12 Entry Points Conservation SSSI Management — Condition, Notifications, Restoration 410+ SSSIs across England, 1.1M hectares. Condition assessments — favourable, unfavourable recovering/declining, part destroyed. Notification under WCA 1981 s.28. Operations consent (s.28E) for agriculture, forestry, recreation. Restoration plans for degraded sites. Landowner partnerships. Threat detection — pollution, invasive species, development. AI satellite and drone monitoring. Landscape AONB Protection — Designated Landscape Management 34 AONBs covering 18% of England. Management plans under CROW Act 2000. Conservation boards for larger AONBs. Development management — great weight to landscape beauty. Dark sky reserves. Tranquillity mapping. Farming in protected landscapes. Tourism pressure management. Climate adaptation. Heritage coast integration. Recovery Nature Recovery Networks — Connectivity, LNRS LNRS under Environment Act 2021 — 48 areas covering all of England. Nature Recovery Network mapping — core areas, corridors, stepping stones. Biodiversity opportunity areas. Ecological connectivity modelling. Wildlife corridor identification. Habitat fragmentation analysis. Integration with BNG and planning. Climate-resilient network design. Biodiversity Biodiversity Net Gain — Metric 4.0, 30-Year Monitoring Mandatory 10% BNG under Environment Act 2021 for major developments. Metric 4.0 — condition, distinctiveness, strategic significance, connectivity. On-site, off-site, credit delivery routes. 30-year management obligations. BNG register. Irreplaceable habitats — ancient woodland, blanket bog. Statutory credits as last resort. Small site exemption. Species Protected Species Licensing — EPS, Mitigation EPS licensing under Habitats & Species Regulations 2017. Species — bats, great crested newts, dormice, badgers, otters, reptiles. Mitigation licences (A10/16). Disturbance and killing offences. Development licence derogation test. Survey methodology best practice. Compensation and mitigation strategies. White-clawed crayfish. Invasive alien species management. Access Access & Open Country — CRoW, Coast Path CRoW Act 2000 access land — mountain, moor, heath, down, common land. Section 16 agreements. Right to roam provisions. Byways and restricted byways. Diversions for land management. Coastal access — England Coast Path under Marine & Coastal Access Act 2009. Access improvement funding. Dog access restrictions. Marine Marine Conservation — MCZs, Seabirds, Blue Carbon Marine Conservation Zones under Marine & Coastal Access Act 2009. Offshore SSSIs (cSACs/pSACs). Designated features — habitats, species, geological. Fisheries management within MCZs. Seabird colonies — SPA designation. Intertidal surveys. Underwater noise impacts. Blue carbon habitats — seagrass, saltmarsh, kelp. Marine litter monitoring. Reserves National Nature Reserves — 224 NNRs, Research 224 NNRs covering 107,000 hectares. Management under National Parks Act 1949. Research partnerships with UKCEH and universities. Long-term ecological monitoring datasets. Public access and engagement. Flagship species recovery — corncrake, bittern, lady's slipper orchid. Wild Ennerdale and rewilding pilots. Agriculture Agri-Environment Schemes — CS, SFI, ES Legacy Environmental Stewardship legacy — ELS, HLS, OELS. Countryside Stewardship — mid/higher
